svg.title: The guide's head in fur, drawn over the shared head part so the rig keeps ONE head geometry: same cranium box, same eye line, same width envelope as every human character, in the beaver's pelt, with the muzzle it carries: a broad pale snout pad with cheek pouches, a wide flat nose and the two big incisors. The muzzle is part of THIS frame rather than its own, because this part already draws under `face` - the same four expressions, brow, pupil and mouth shape, play on the guide as on every human character - and a second frame would have cost the shared atlas a page it did not need. The incisors are deliberately larger than life: they are the second of the two features that carry the identification at phone size, and exaggerating an identifying feature is simplification (art bible 5). Flat crown, heavy cheeks and small round ears set LOW and well back at the side of the skull - the arrangement in assets/refs/beaver/beaver-head-and-forepaws.jpg. High rounded ears would read as a bear, which is the mistake this shape was redrawn to fix. Cartoon proportions are identical for every character (docs/content-review.md 6), and this part is how an animal companion joins that canon instead of getting its own.
